issues.description: download_and_untar.sh swallows missing-unzip error instead of failing
issues.detail: The script checks for unzip and merely echoes a warning, then proceeds under set -euo pipefail to invoke unzip anyway. The precondition 'unzip is installed' is asserted and immediately violated without termination. Either exit non-zero on the check, or remove the check entirely. As written, the guard is theater.

issues.description: Usage block prints but does not exit, violating the stated argument precondition
issues.detail: When argc is out of [1,2], the script prints usage and falls through to realpath $1, which will crash or, worse, succeed silently with the wrong frame. A precondition violation must terminate. Add 'exit 1' after the heredoc. This is the canonical defensive-as-substitute failure: a message where a refusal was required.

issues.description: Unquoted realpath arguments break under whitespace or empty values
issues.detail: realpath $1 and realpath ${2:-$extract_dir} are unquoted under set -u. Any path containing a space splits into multiple words; the postcondition 'extract_dir is a single absolute path' is unestablished. Quote them: "$(realpath "$1")". The same discipline is absent from numerous awk/sed pipelines downstream in data.sh.

issues.description: data.sh transcript filter is a chain of brittle sed substitutions with no stated invariant
issues.detail: The pipeline strips a hand-picked set of full-width punctuation and one Cyrillic-looking 'A' via successive sed calls. There is no specification of which characters are legal in the postcondition text, no invariant tying the filter to the tokenizer's expected alphabet, and no termination argument that the set is complete. This is folklore, not reasoning. Document the target alphabet or normalize via a single explicit table.

issues.description: utt.list is overwritten mid-pipeline, destroying the invariant it was created to maintain
issues.detail: Line 46 writes utt.list from wav.flist; line 51 overwrites utt.list from transcripts.txt. The two files denote different sets and the second silently shadows the first. Any later reader assuming 'utt.list = utterances with audio' is wrong. Use distinct names; the cost of a second filename is negligible compared to the confusion of the same name meaning two things.

issues.description: README links to a path that does not exist in the recipe
issues.detail: The README advertises ./conf/train/train_asr_branchformer_e24_amp.yaml, but the file actually lives at ./conf/train_asr_branchformer_e24_amp.yaml. Small, but exactly the sort of careless inconsistency that signals the author did not re-read what was written. Reason about what you publish.

review.summary: The recipe is conventional and the results table is honest, but the supporting shell is unreasoned. download_and_untar.sh advertises preconditions it does not enforce: a missing unzip is merely announced, and an argc violation prints usage then falls through into realpath of an unquoted possibly-empty argument. data.sh's text normalization is a folkloric chain of sed substitutions with no stated target alphabet, and it overloads the filename utt.list to mean two different sets within the same function. None of this is fatal to training, but none of it is reasoned. TESTED-NOT-PROVED: the CER table is offered where preconditions and invariants were required.
